question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y={x}^{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{sec}⁡x\,\operatorname{ln}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\ \frac{1}{y}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =(\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\operatorname{sec}⁡x)\operatorname{ln}⁡x+\operatorname{sec}⁡x(\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\ \frac{1}{y}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =(\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x)\operatorname{ln}⁡x+\operatorname{sec}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =y(\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x+\frac{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y={x}^{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={x}^{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x+\frac{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}{x}) \\  & ={x}^{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}{x}\cdot (x\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\operatorname{tan}⁡x+1) \\  & ={x}^{\operatorname{sec}⁡x-1}\operatorname{sec}⁡x\cdot (x\operatorname{ln}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x+1).\end{aligned}
$$
